meta.caveat: This Mac has a heterogeneous CPU (performance + efficiency cores) and macOS gives no CPU affinity control, so 'N threads' means N worker threads whose cores are chosen by the OS scheduler. 4 threads equals the number of performance cores but is not guaranteed to run on them; multi-thread numbers are noisier than single-thread ones. Tiny models can be slower with more threads (synchronisation overhead). An Apple CPU is not an edge-device CPU, so absolute latencies are a relative comparison between models, not deployment predictions.
meta.weights_used: fold 1 only (D-40): latency does not depend on the trained weights
meta.pruned_variant: s70 only (unstructured sparsity, dense fp32 eager execution)
meta.aggregation: median over repeats of each repeat's median / p95; spread_pct = (max-min)/median of the repeat medians; noisy = spread > 10 %
meta.thread_settings: torch.set_num_threads(n) and ONNX Runtime intra_op_num_threads=n; n in (1, 4); OMP_NUM_THREADS unset
